name: Fossil brown bear (left pyramidal bone)
description:
3D scan of the left pyramidal bone of a  fossil brown bear (*Ursus arctos*). 


Fossil of a prime adult female skull of brown bear. The specimen was found in "Abisso Oriano Coltelli" cave (44°05'35,0 N, 10°14'47,0" E, labelled T/Lu 642 in the Tuscan register of caves) which opens at 1209 m a.s.l on the western slope of "Monte Alto di Sella" (Apuan Alps). The mammal assemblage collected consists of 486 investigated specimens, 127 of which belong to an individual skeleton of brown bear. The bear died from non-violent causes, probably during hibernation. The specimen was dated providing a conventional age of 6480 ± 40 14 C ka BP (Holocene).
More information : https://amq.aiqua.it/index.php/amq/article/view/112


Specimen: Brown bear, *Ursus arctos* Linnaeus, 1758

Inventory number: I17771

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

name: indian cattle leech overview
description:
The Indian cattle leech (Hirudinaria granulosa) is a large freshwater annelid commonly found in ponds, lakes, and slow-moving waters across India and South Asia. It belongs to Phylum Annelida and Class Hirudinea.

This species is an ectoparasite, feeding on the blood of cattle and other vertebrates. The body is elongated, dorsoventrally flattened, and divided into segments. It possesses:

Anterior sucker – Used for attachment and feeding

Posterior sucker – Helps in locomotion and firm attachment

Muscular body wall – Enables looping movement

No setae (bristles) – Unlike other annelids

Leeches secrete hirudin, an anticoagulant that prevents blood clotting during feeding. Respiration occurs through the body surface.

This model is useful for studying annelid morphology, parasitic adaptations, and comparative invertebrate anatomy.
